CHIEF COMPLAINT
Ankle injury

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Jerry is a 45-year-old male who presents with a right ankle injury sustained while playing basketball with his son today. Patient was going for a shot when his son collided with him while going for a rebound. Patient landed awkwardly on the ankle, rolled and twisted it. He reports pain on the outside of the ankle with visible bruising and swelling. He has been having trouble walking and reports the ankle does not feel stable or solid. Patient recently returned to working out and was in a good rhythm at the gym prior to this injury. He also volunteered to coach basketball starting in April.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

MEDICATIONS
Meloxicam (newly prescribed)

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Son Sean, age 10, plays basketball.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works from home and is able to elevate ankle regularly. He has dogs at home. He plays basketball recreationally with his son and recently returned to regular workouts at the gym. He has volunteered to coach basketball starting in April.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Right ankle with swelling on the lateral side. Exquisite tenderness over the lateral ankle with palpation. Some tenderness noted over the medial deltoid region. Skin intact with no epidermolysis. Brisk capillary refill. No malalignment noted. Patient is able to stand on the ankle but reports difficulty walking and instability.

RESULTS
X-ray of right ankle (AP, lateral, and oblique views): Displaced lateral malleolus fracture at the Weber C level. No evidence of medial or posterior malleolar fractures. Fracture noted to be somewhat unstable in position.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Lateral malleolar fracture of the right ankle. Recommended treatment is surgical fixation with plate and screws. Patient expected to be out of activity for approximately three months but may continue with coaching starting in April. Crutches to be provided. Meloxicam prescribed to help with swelling. Patient instructed to ice the ankle and keep it elevated. Plan to return to exercise within three months post-surgery.
